 $ $$$ Budget Price tier: Budget Check price 
 Before you choose
 Can a Power Station Run a Space Heater? Runtime Math and Smarter Ways to Stay Warm in an Outage (2026) 
 RV & Vanlife Power Sizing: How Many Watt-Hours Do You Actually Need? (2026) 
 What Size Power Station to Run a Refrigerator? Runtime Math That Actually Works (2026) 
 If your gas furnace dies with the grid, the problem is not the fuel. The burner needs electricity for a blower, an igniter and a control board, and without them the house gets cold even though the gas is still flowing. A portable power station can supply that electricity, and the load is small enough to make it a good use of a battery. The harder question is how to connect it, because most furnaces are not plug-in appliances. This guide covers wattage, runtime and safe hookup. For the wider checklist, including the fridge, CPAP, solar and cold-weather storage, see our winter storm prep guide , which this post does not repeat.
 Prices and specs are from our database as of October 2026. Check the current price before you buy. We are not electricians, and nothing here replaces a licensed electrician’s advice or your local code.
 Can a power station run a gas furnace?
 For the blower and controls, yes. A gas or propane furnace burns fuel for heat and uses electricity to move air, light the burner and run its safety circuits. That is a small slice of the energy a resistive heater needs. As our space heater guide shows, a 1,500W heater drains a 2kWh station in about an hour, while a furnace blower can run for many hours on the same battery.
 What a power station cannot do is run an electric furnace , electric heat strips or a heat pump’s backup heat. Those draw thousands of watts at 240V. Even the largest units we track would empty in well under an hour or two, and most stations cannot deliver that power at all. If your home heats with electricity, a power station is the wrong tool for whole-house heat.
 How many watts does a gas furnace blower use?
 There is no single answer, and we will not give you a made-up one. The draw depends on the blower motor type, the speed the furnace selects, and the furnace size. As a rough guide from general knowledge, many blower motors fall somewhere between a hundred and several hundred watts while running, with older permanent-split-capacitor motors tending to draw more than newer variable-speed ones. The igniter pulls power only briefly at the start of each cycle, and the control board and thermostat add a small constant load.
 Find yours rather than guessing:
 Read the nameplate. It lists the furnace’s rated amps and volts. Multiply them for volt-amps, which is an upper bound on what the whole furnace can draw.
 Measure it. An energy meter on a cord-and-plug furnace, or a clamp meter used by an electrician on the supply, shows real watts and how often the blower runs during a cold day.
 Note the duty cycle. In a cold, leaky house the furnace runs more than in a mild one, so measure in cold weather if you can.
 Check for 240V. Most gas furnaces run on 120V, but confirm on the nameplate. A 240V furnace needs a station with 240V output.
 Our winter storm prep guide uses a 400W blower running 40 percent of the time as a worked illustration. That is an assumption to show the method, not a typical figure.
 How long will a power station run a furnace blower?
 Use the same formula as everywhere on this site: runtime in hours = battery Wh x 0.85 / average watts . “Average” is what matters, because the blower cycles. A blower that draws 400W while running and runs half the time averages about 200W. Here is the arithmetic for four stations in our database at three averages:
 Station Capacity Output (surge) At 100W average At 200W average At 400W average 
 Anker SOLIX C1000 1,056Wh 1,800W (2,400W) about 9 hours about 4.5 hours about 2.2 hours 
 Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 2,048Wh 2,400W (4,000W) about 17 hours about 8.7 hours about 4.4 hours 
 Anker SOLIX F3800 3,840Wh 6,000W (9,000W) about 33 hours about 16 hours about 8.2 hours 
 EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 4,096Wh 4,000W (8,000W) about 35 hours about 17 hours about 8.7 hours 
 These are best-case figures. Batteries lose some usable capacity in the cold, and our RV and van life guide suggests budgeting 10 to 20 percent less. They also assume the furnace is the only load. In a real outage, the fridge, which our outage scenarios guide puts at about 1,200Wh a day, shares the same battery. A 2kWh station at a 100W furnace average plus a fridge covers roughly a night, not a long weekend.
 Multi-day outages are a solar or expansion problem, not a bigger-blower problem. The F3800 expands to 26.9kWh in our data and the DELTA Pro 3 to 12kWh, and our solar pairing guide covers refilling in winter, when yield is a fraction of summer. For the sizing method, see what size power station do I need .
 Is a furnace plug-in or hardwired?
 Most residential furnaces are hardwired to a dedicated circuit, with the power supplied through a junction box on or near the furnace, usually with a service switch nearby. That is why “can I just plug it in?” has the answer “no” in most homes. Some furnaces, especially certain manufactured-home or smaller units, use a cord and plug, but you should not assume yours does. Check the furnace itself and the manual, and ask a pro if you are unsure.
 The two things to avoid are the same ones our space heater guide warns about:
 Do not run an extension cord to a hardwired furnace’s junction box. Splicing into a furnace’s wiring yourself is a fire and shock risk and can void the furnace’s listing.
 Do not back-feed your panel by plugging a station into a wall outlet with a male-to-male cord. It can energize lines you thought were dead, endangering utility workers and anyone touching a circuit, and it bypasses breaker protection.
 What is the safe way to connect a power station to a furnace?
 The safe options all involve a licensed electrician:
 Manual transfer switch. A small subpanel takes over selected circuits, such as the furnace, fridge and a few outlets, and switches them from the grid to the station through an inlet. It keeps the house isolated from the utility.
 Interlock kit on the main panel. A mechanical plate prevents the main breaker and the backup breaker from being on at the same time. It is usually the cheaper route when your panel supports it, but it needs the right panel model and a proper inlet.
 A purpose-built home backup kit. Some power station makers sell their own transfer panels or home-integration systems. Compatibility depends on your station and your panel, so check the maker’s documentation. We have not verified any particular kit here.
 Questions to ask your electrician:
 Which circuits will the backup feed, and how many watts will they total?
 Does your station’s output match what the switch expects (120V only, or 240V split-phase)?
 Does the install need a permit and an inspection?
 How should the station’s neutral and ground be handled so the system is safe? Stations differ, so have them check your model’s manual.
 Where will the station sit? Indoors and dry, not in a freezing garage. Our indoor, UPS and EPS safety guide covers placement.
 The 240V question matters. In our database, the Anker SOLIX F3800 and BLUETTI Apex 300 list 120V/240V split-phase output. Most other units are 120V only, which suits a 120V furnace but not a 240V one.
 Will a furnace work on a power station’s output?
 Mostly. Stations produce household-style AC, so a standard blower and control board run normally. Check that the nameplate amps times volts sit comfortably under the station’s continuous rating, and remember a blower draws more for a moment at startup, so confirm the surge need with your electrician or the manual. A furnace on a transfer switch also loses power briefly at changeover and restarts its sequence, so expect a short delay before the burner relights.
 What about carbon monoxide and gas safety?
 A power station has no exhaust, which is its main safety advantage over a generator. A furnace is another matter: it burns fuel and has to vent properly. Before winter:
 Have working carbon monoxide and smoke alarms with battery backup.
 Have the furnace and its vent serviced by a qualified technician, as you would any year.
 Never run a gas oven, grill, camp stove or fuel heater indoors for warmth. If anyone has a headache, dizziness or nausea while fuel is burning, get to fresh air and call emergency services.
 Never run a generator in or next to the home as a substitute. Our power station vs generator guide compares the two.
 Which power station is best for a gas furnace?
 Pick on capacity and voltage, then connection:
 Anker SOLIX F3800 : 3,840Wh and 6,000W with 120V/240V output, so it can serve a 240V furnace from one unit. At 132 lb it is a stay-put unit. Our data notes street prices are frequently $1,800 to $2,200 against a $3,999 list.
 EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 : the largest battery we track at 4,096Wh and 4,000W, with fast solar input for daily refills. It costs $3,199 to $3,699 in our data.
 Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 : 2,048Wh and 2,400W at about 41.7 lb. It is a sensible middle choice for a night or two of a modest blower plus a fridge.
 Anker SOLIX C1000 : 1,056Wh and 1,800W. It is the budget option for a small, efficient blower overnight, with little left over for the fridge.
 For a head-to-head on the top two, read DELTA Pro 3 vs SOLIX F3800 .
 Should you buy before Black Friday?
 If your furnace is the only heat in the house, buy and have the install done before the first cold snap, not after the forecast. Electricians get busy and stock slips once a storm is in the news. Black Friday is November 27, 2026, and Cyber Monday is November 30. We have not verified any 2026 offers, and our power station Black Friday guide shows what was reported in November 2025 and how to judge a deal. If you can wait, note today’s price and compare. Do not forget the electrician’s cost, which a sale on the station does not reduce.
 Bottom line
 A portable power station can keep a gas furnace’s blower and controls running for hours, and it is a far better use of a battery than a space heater. The condition is a safe connection. If your furnace is hardwired, as most are, hire a licensed electrician for a transfer switch or interlock, and never improvise with extension cords or back-feeding. Measure your furnace’s real draw, use Wh x 0.85 / average watts to size the battery, remember the fridge shares it, and check today’s price rather than the sale badge.
 Don't guess. Calculate.

 Frequently asked questions
 Can a portable power station run a gas furnace? It can power the blower motor, igniter and control board of a gas or propane furnace, which together are a modest load compared with resistive heat. The practical obstacle is the connection: most furnaces are hardwired to a dedicated circuit, so a licensed electrician needs to install a transfer switch or interlock. Check your nameplate for the actual draw.
 How many watts does a gas furnace use? It varies by furnace. Blower motors range from roughly 100 to several hundred watts and sometimes more, depending on the motor type and speed, and the igniter and controls add a small amount. Read the furnace nameplate for amps and multiply by the voltage, or measure with an energy meter during cold weather. Do not rely on a generic number.
 Can I plug my furnace into a power station with an extension cord? Not unless the furnace is a cord-and-plug model designed for it, which is uncommon. Do not run an extension cord to a hardwired furnace's junction box, and do not plug the station into a wall outlet to back-feed a circuit. Both are dangerous and can energize utility lines or start fires. Use a transfer switch or interlock installed by a licensed electrician.
 Do I need a transfer switch or interlock? If your furnace is hardwired, yes, in most cases. Transfer equipment keeps the house circuit isolated from the grid while the station feeds it. Local code and permit rules differ, and the right device depends on your panel and your station, so ask a licensed electrician before you buy.
 How long will a 2,000Wh power station run a furnace? Use runtime = Wh x 0.85 / average watts. At an average of 200W, which blends the blower running and idle time, a 2,048Wh station gives about 8.7 hours. At 100W it is about 17 hours, at 400W about 4.4 hours. Remember the fridge and other loads share the same battery.
 Can a power station run an electric furnace or heat pump? Not for any useful time. Electric furnaces and strip heat draw thousands of watts at 240V, and heat pumps with backup strips can too. A 6,000W unit like the Anker SOLIX F3800 can deliver the power briefly, but no portable battery can sustain it for long. For those systems, plan a different backup or heat source.
